overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by entering executive session under Purpose 8 to receive an update on a harbormaster screening process it could not lawfully discuss there, and ordered compliance and minutes release.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board entered executive session under Purpose 8 (applicant screening) without a valid statutory purpose, including to receive a screening committee update.
allegations.key_passage: Thus, the Board could not invoke Purpose 8 for this discussion.

allegations.summary: To the extent the complaint alleged the preliminary screening committee had already chosen a single harbormaster candidate, the AG found the process was still ongoing.
allegations.key_passage: our in camera review of the executive session minutes indicates that the process was ongoing

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.

Release to the public of the February 27, 2017 executive session minutes for the portion not held for a proper purpose, within 30 days of receipt of the letter, without redaction or withholding based on privilege or Public Records Law exemptions (portions still protected by a valid ongoing executive session purpose may be withheld).
remedy_passage: We order the Board's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law. Because the portion of the February 27, 2017 executive session addressed in this letter was not held for a proper purpose, we order the release to the public of those executive session minutes within thirty (30) days of receipt of this letter.
